data.title: BCG vaccine
data.summary: VII Vaccines · Live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis (Bacille Calmette–Guérin) vaccine
data.body:
_Injectables · VII Vaccines_

**Class:** Live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis (Bacille Calmette–Guérin) vaccine

## Mechanism of action
- Induces cell-mediated (Th1) immunity to mycobacteria
- Protects children against severe TB (miliary TB, TB meningitis); variable protection against pulmonary TB and some protection against leprosy
- Non-specific immune stimulation (trained immunity) — basis for use in warts and bladder cancer

## Pharmacokinetics
- 0.1 mL intradermal (0.05 mL in infants under 1 month) over the left deltoid insertion
- Papule → pustule → ulcer → scar over 6–12 weeks

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Routine at birth in India (national schedule; up to 1 year of age)
- Dermatology: immunotherapy for warts (intralesional or intradermal), leprosy contacts (some programmes)
- Intravesical BCG for superficial bladder cancer

## Dose & formulations
- 0.1 mL intradermal (0.05 mL under 1 month)
- Warts (off-label protocols): 0.1 mL intradermal/IL every 2–4 weeks for a few sessions

## Adverse effects
- Normal: local papule, ulcer, scar
- Complications: large ulcer, abscess, suppurative lymphadenitis (BCG adenitis), keloid
- Cutaneous TB at the site: lupus vulgaris, scrofuloderma; tuberculids (lichen scrofulosorum, papulonecrotic)
- Disseminated BCG infection (BCGosis) in immunodeficient children (SCID, chronic granulomatous disease, IFN-γ pathway defects, HIV)
- Flare (redness) of an old BCG scar in Kawasaki disease (a diagnostic clue)

## Contraindications
- Immunosuppression (primary immunodeficiency, symptomatic HIV, steroids, biologics, chemotherapy)
- Pregnancy; generalised skin disease or infection at the site; active TB

## Drug interactions
- Antituberculous drugs inactivate the vaccine
- Immunosuppressants increase the risk of disseminated infection

## Monitoring
- Check the site at follow-up; investigate persistent ulcer or adenitis

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (live vaccine).

## Viva points
- Live vaccine — intradermal, left deltoid
- Cutaneous complications include lupus vulgaris and scrofuloderma at the site
- BCGosis signals immunodeficiency
- BCG scar reactivation in Kawasaki disease

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.43 (IL immunotherapy for warts — brief); national immunisation schedule; Khopkar (Immunobiologicals). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
